transcript:
Meeting header:
Date/Time: 2027-01-21 15:00 UTC
Duration: 38 minutes
Attendees: Alex Duarte, Samir Patel, Maya Chen (Redwood) - Dr. Erin Walsh, Luis Fernandez, Sophie Li (VistaMed)

[00:00] Alex Duarte: okay good afternoon everyone, thanks for joining, um this is Alex from Redwood, i'm the AE on the account, with samir and maya from the success and solutions teams. quick roll call?
[00:10] Dr. Erin Walsh: hi erin here, CTO at vista med.
[00:14] Luis Fernandez: luis, it is it ops.
[00:17] Sophie Li: sophie product. thanks.
[00:20] Samir Patel: hi all, samir, csm, i'll be your primary contact for onboarding.
[00:24] Maya Chen: maya, solutions eng, i'll own the performance and infra bits.
[00:30] Alex Duarte: great. quick agenda - goals for pilot, current infra and constraints, security/compliance checklist, pilot timeline and next steps. sound good?
[00:36] Erin: yup sounds good.
[02:15] Erin: to start, our top priority is that any inference touching patient data needs to stay within our VPC and comply with HIPAA - we want to understand private deployment options and networking. second, latency threshold, our triage endpoint should be under 200 milliseconds median, peak 99th under 800ms ideally.
[02:40] Maya Chen: understood. for those constraints we typically recommend private deployment (VPC) or dedicated - private if you need control over KMS and egress. dedicated is good if you want reserved capacity but still use our control plane.
[03:05] Luis: question - for private, do you run control plane on your side or redwood's? we need to keep everything on-prem or in our cloud for compliance.
[03:18] Samir Patel: good q - the private option gives you a customer-managed control plane, you host the control plane components in your VPC, redwood provides the package. we can also do an air-gapped install for very strict environments.
[03:35] Luis: okay that's promising. how about KMS and secrets?
[03:40] Maya Chen: you can integrate your KMS/HSM for model keys and disk encryption; we support AWS KMS and common HSM vendors, and you control the keys. keys never leave your VPC in private mode.
[04:05] Erin: perfect. on the workloads side, our initial pilot is classification + triage on clinical notes, about 10k req/day, peak 50 req/sec, mostly short context length ~512 tokens.
[04:25] Alex Duarte: that helps - 50 req/sec with 512 tokens is doable on a small dedicated pool; for sub-200ms median we may need batching tuned and smaller model variant or quantized profile.
[04:40] Sophie: what about model privacy, are you hosting models or pulling from an open catalog? we need assurance models are not shipped with telemetry.
[04:48] Maya Chen: you can bring your own model or pick a verified open-model from our catalog; in private mode models live in your infrastructure. no telemetry leaves without your opt-in. there can be subtlety with telemetry we use for health checks but it's optional.
[05:20] Erin: SOC2 is a requirement, do you have SOC2 and can you share the report?
[05:26] Samir Patel: yes we are SOC2 Type II - we'll share the pack, plus our ISO docs. expect that in the security pack we send after this call.
[07:00] Luis: let's talk networking specifics, firewall rules, peering, nat gateways - we need a list to show our security team.
[07:10] Maya Chen: i'll produce a minimal inbound/outbound port list and example peering setup, plus ip ranges for dedicated pools. for private installs we give you terraform modules to spin up the control plane.
[07:25] Luis: terraform modules is good. can you support our SSO provider? we use Okta, SAML 2.0.
[07:31] Samir Patel: yes, SAML/Okta is standard. we support SCIM provisioning and RBAC. we'll need an Okta contact to finish setup.
[08:05] Erin: timeline - we'd like pilot to start early feb, two week validation, then scale by mid-march. is that realistic?
[08:15] Alex Duarte: yes that's doable. typical onboarding path: week 0 - kick off and infra prep, week 1 - deploy private/dedicated, week 2 - run benchmarks and integrate, week 3-4 - pilot validation. so feb start works if we get network artifacts this week.
[09:00] Sophie: pricing question - for dedicated pilot, do you do short-term commits or month-to-month?
[09:06] Alex Duarte: we have flexible pilots - 30 day reserved trial pricing for dedicated; for long-term we do monthly/annual commits with discounts. i'll send numbers after this call.
[12:30] Erin: performance - maya, any initial thought on model choices and quantization to meet latency?
[12:40] Maya Chen: given 512 tokens and 50 rps peak, i'd suggest a smaller LLM tuned for classification or a 7B family with int8 quantization on A100 or equivalent; we'll run latency tests and provide a recommended config. continuous batching will help reduce cost while keeping median latency target.
[13:10] Luis: can we run benchmarks with our actual payload? we don't want synthetic tests.
[13:20] Maya Chen: absolutely, we request a sanitized sample prompt set and we'll run it on a dedicated trial pool. need 200-500 representative samples for a good baseline.
[14:00] Sophie: security again - audit logs and data retention policy? we need logs for 12 months and ability to export.
[14:08] Samir Patel: audit logs are available, and retention can be extended as an add-on. exports and SIEM integration via S3 are supported.
[19:00] Erin: any blockers from regulatory side? data residency - our data must stay in us-east-1.
[19:08] Maya Chen: we can pin regions for both dedicated and private deployments; for private it's in your VPC so residency satisfied. we also support regional deployment of model artifacts.
[26:00] Luis: what about fallback and high availability? if a node fails during triage traffic, how graceful is degradation?
[26:12] Maya Chen: runtime includes smart routing and automatic fallback to compatible model variants, and we can configure multi-availability-zone pools and autoscaling; HA is part of the dedicated SLA.
[33:30] Alex Duarte: recap - action items we discussed: i'll send onboarding checklist, pricing, and security pack; maya will run benchmarks with sample dataset; luis will provide network and sso contacts. schedule scoping 2027-01-28 to decide private vs dedicated. any other questions?
[33:50] Erin: no, that covers it. thanks.
[37:30] Alex Duarte: great thanks everyone, we'll follow up via email with the pack and calendar invite.
[37:50] Call ended: 15:38 UTC

Notes: transcription has mild errors in names and can mis-hear acronyms. Links referenced: onboarding-checklist (link sent after call), security-pack (to be shared), benchmark-results (to be shared by maya).
